product_name: L-Shaped Memory-Foam Forearm & Wrist Desk Rest Pad (black)

target_buyer.description: A desk worker (programmer, office employee, or gamer) whose forearm and wrist rest on a hard, sharp desk edge for hours a day and who has already decided a dedicated pad is the fix — now choosing between the L-shaped pads on page one
target_buyer.context: Mid-workday or mid-session, arm aching or going numb at the desk edge; shopping on a phone or second monitor, comparing three or four look-alike L-shaped pads by photo, price and reviews

must_keep: Black color only — one SKU color, no variants
L-shaped extension: a lip that folds over and stays in contact with the desk's front edge so the arm never meets the edge
High-density foam core (not a soft cheap sponge)
Good fabric (fiber) cover — comfortable, breathable, easy to clean
Designed for at least 5 years of daily use — durability engineered, not claimed
Normal, simple packaging — spend on the product, not the box
Shelf price between $15 and $25 with a 30-40% margin
must_avoid: A design that only survives the first few months (peeling base, flattening foam, tacky cover)

packaging_note: Founder wants normal packaging, nothing premium. The supplier's existing box is a plain kraft mailer, 32 x 11 x 6.5 cm, for a 2-piece set (590 g/set), 30 sets per 58 x 34 x 43 cm carton. Keep it simple-tier: kraft box or sleeve plus one printed card. Put the money into durability, not the unboxing.
user_hypotheses: A black, L-shaped forearm-and-wrist pad can beat the three liked page-one listings (EdgeRest, ArmCloud, JIKIOU) at a $15-25 shelf price while holding a 30-40% margin
A cheaper factory than the one quoted (EXW USD 7.58/pc, USD 5.75/set-of-2 without logo, mold USD 230, MOQ 300) exists for the same spec, and the saving is what makes the 30-40% margin possible

Buyers will pay inside the $15-25 band for a visibly more durable, futuristic-looking pad that is easier to clean and more relaxing for wrist and elbow than the current L-shaped pads, as long as the price stays under the band ceiling
assumptions: FOCUS MODE: only 3 named product(s); no category sweep

The founder has no listing yet, so none of the three focus products is 'mine'. The product under evaluation is the founder's planned launch, described by the supplier's sample: an L-shaped foldable memory-foam pad with a milk-silk fabric cover, 300 x 100 x 20 mm, about 250 g per piece, sold as a 2-piece set. All three focus products are the grid the buyer sees and the bar to beat.

Supplier quote on file (reference only, from 'Ahmad'): EXW USD 7.58/pc as a single, roughly USD 5.75 per 2-piece set without logo, mold cost USD 230, MOQ 300 pcs. Genius must treat these as the real cost baseline instead of inventing BOM estimates, and should show what landed cost the 30-40% margin target actually requires at each price point in the band.

The previous category-mode run (runs/elbow-forearm-desk-rest-pad) established the arena: page-one prices $8-21 with a ~$15.50 median, VAYDEER leading at 2,045 reviews, complaint clusters C1 'still feel the desk edge' (35%), C2 'cover turns sticky / smells' (30%), C3 'base or mount fails' (20%). That run reached FIX-FIRST because its estimated economics gave only a 6% contribution; this run replaces estimates with the supplier's real quote.
The first URL the founder pasted (an Amazon search for 'bearing adjust speed jump rope') is unrelated to this product and was treated as a mis-paste; it was not researched.
Color is fixed to black by the founder, so color strategy is about finish, texture and the one accent that makes a black pad legible in a grid, not about choosing a color.
